label: The ~12 absent-carrier bound is refuted by the generator's own build: a live buildIndex over the current corpus yields exactly 199 owners for 'feature specification', identical to the committed artifact (set diffs empty in both directions); the iteration-8 207-vs-199 gap compared an rg line-pattern count against an index owner set, not drift. The real staleness is manifest-level: manifestHash differs, indexed paths 13,460 -> 13,465 and unique phrases 34,176 -> 34,179 since the 2026-10-06 freeze, with zero template-phrase discrepancy.

A Gate 1 scope is pin-safe but not simply adopted: the byte-pinned delivery receipts (f-iter001-006) and frozen GATE_3_QUESTION arrays (f-iter003-002) constrain Gate 3, not Gate 1, and no test pins the lookup invocation text; the blockers are 20+ documented invocation copies, Gate 1 executing before Gate 3 (no folder exists for new work), and scoping suppressing the very cross-packet sibling evidence the placement decision needs (iteration-8: unscoped 20 documents vs track-scoped 2 vs packet-scoped 0). Adoption is a resume/context-relevance device, not a first-write noise fix.

f-iter008-002's blanket advisory-only constraint on fail-loud is over-broad: inv-iter002-001 is explicitly scoped to list_recent_track_packets, and create.sh already fails the scaffold loudly on template-contract drift (contract helpers console.error + exit 3; consumer converts to exit 1 under set -euo pipefail), so a seeder drift check against the template source may fail loud; only packet-state checks stay idempotent return 0. The additive-union reconciliation verdict stands; the constraint wording does not.

Manifest staleness and per-phrase loss are independent signals: a rebuild is all-or-nothing and manifestHash folds corpus hash, exclusions, ignored paths and counts, while postings regenerate wholesale, so a stale artifact can be behind on the manifest and exactly in sync on any phrase's owner set; freshness is judged by manifest/--check comparison, never by spot-checking a phrase.
